issue.title: Redact private bead-attachment descriptor metadata behind a mixed-fleet reader gate

task_type_fields.proposal:
Redact private bead-attachment descriptor metadata (research report `research:202609/bead_attachment_audience/bead_attachment_audience.md` section 5.3), so a private attachment's descriptor stops exposing its name, sha256, and size to everyone who can read the bead store.

Today, since sase-1d5 GA, `visibility: private` protects only the bytes. Descriptors on the bead wire (`BeadNoteAttachmentWire` in sase-core `note_attachment/manifest.rs`) still carry `name`, `sha256`, `size_bytes`, and `mime_type`, and the rendered notes keep `@attachment:<name>` tokens. `docs/beads.md` and the attach/note `--help` say so plainly: "private protects bytes, not names or prose".

Old readers require `sha256` on every descriptor, so redaction needs a mixed-fleet reader gate. First land a reader that tolerates redacted descriptors, then gate writers on fleet readiness. It also has to settle how the manifest/token one-to-one validation rule and the roster/references queries treat redacted entries. This work belongs in sase-core (wire and validation) with thin Python callers.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: Proposed by sase-1d5.8 (ga phase of epic sase-1d5, PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP #1). Settled design decision 10 of plan:202609/public_bead_attachments.md deferred it deliberately: it is orthogonal to public-by-default, and it needs a wire-compatibility gate the epic did not budget for.

issue.creation_reason: sase-1d5 shipped public-by-default attachments but deferred private descriptor redaction; names, digests, and sizes of private attachments stay visible to bead readers until this lands.

payload.description: Epic whose settled design decision 10 deferred this redaction; ga phase sase-1d5.8 proposed it
